blocks.md: A quadratic form is a way of building a single number from a vector using a matrix — the multivariable version of a number times x squared. A matrix is positive definite if that number is positive for every nonzero vector, like a bowl that curves up in every direction. Checking definiteness tells you whether a critical point is a minimum or maximum, and whether a matrix behaves like a variance.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: It is the second-order condition in optimisation, and the reason least squares has a unique minimum.

| Name | Condition for all $\mathbf{x}\neq\mathbf{0}$ | Eigenvalue test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Positive definite (PD) | $\mathbf{x}'A\mathbf{x} > 0$ | all $\lambda > 0$ |
| Positive semidefinite (PSD) | $\mathbf{x}'A\mathbf{x} \geq 0$ | all $\lambda \geq 0$ |
| Negative definite (ND) | $\mathbf{x}'A\mathbf{x} < 0$ | all $\lambda < 0$ |
| Indefinite | takes both signs | mixed signs |
**Leading principal minors test** (PD): the determinants of the top-left $1\times1$, $2\times2$, … submatrices are all positive. For ND they alternate in sign, starting negative.
It equals zero only if $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}$ for some $\mathbf{v}\neq\mathbf{0}$ — i.e. only if the columns are dependent. So $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}$ is **PD exactly under full rank**.

- **Optimization**: second-order conditions — a PD Hessian means a minimum, ND a maximum ([Unconstrained Optimization](note:unconstrained-optimization), [Hessian Matrix](note:hessian-matrix)); convexity ([Convexity and Concavity](note:convexity-and-concavity)).
- **Econometrics**: the OLS Hessian $2\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}$ is PD, so the normal equations give a minimum ([OLS in Matrix Form](note:ols-in-matrix-form)); covariance matrices are PSD; $\mathbf{e}'\mathbf{e} = \boldsymbol{\varepsilon}'\mathbf{M}\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}$ is a quadratic form, which is why its distribution is chi-square ([Sampling Distribution of OLS](note:sampling-distribution-of-ols)).
